whatIs.title: Digital signage, in three sentences.
whatIs.body: A digital sign is a screen that shows what you tell it to — a menu, a price list, an offer, a notice — and changes the moment you change your mind. You need three things: a screen you probably already own, a small player device behind it, and software to control it from anywhere. SignageWall is the third one.

items.q: What do I need to get started?
items.a: A screen, a small player device and an account. The screen can be an ordinary TV you already own. The player is an Android box, a mini-PC or a computer that is already sitting there — you install our app on it, scan the code that appears on screen, and it is paired.

No. If you can make a social media post, you can run a screen. Everything happens in a browser: pick content, choose which screens get it, publish. There is no server to install and nobody has to come out to you.

items.q: What happens when the internet drops?
items.a: The screen carries on showing the last content it downloaded, and syncs again the moment the connection returns. A watchdog restarts the player if it ever stalls, so a frozen screen recovers on its own rather than waiting for someone to notice.

{price} per screen per month up to five screens, with every feature included — a café pays the same rate per screen as a small chain. Above five screens the price is quoted for the size of your network.

items.q: Can I try it before paying?
items.a: Yes — {trialDays} days with everything switched on, no credit card. Nothing is charged automatically when the trial ends; if you do not continue, your content simply waits in the account.

items.q: Can I run just one screen?
items.a: Yes, and many customers do. Nothing about the product is switched off at the low end, and there is no minimum you have to reach before it makes sense.

items.q: Does it work on my existing screens?
items.a: Almost certainly. Any TV, monitor or professional display with an HDMI input works. Purpose-built signage displays earn their price if you run sixteen hours a day or put a screen in direct sunlight — for everything else, an ordinary TV lasts years.

items.q: How many screens can I manage?
items.a: One to several hundred, from the same dashboard. Screens group by location so you publish to a group rather than to devices one at a time, which is the difference that starts to matter around screen number ten.
